fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Sun and Star Cards Frame the Episode", "body": "Chance Garton explained that he pairs two Major Arcana cards with each episode, and that he first guessed the Hierophant before settling on the Sun alongside the Star. He described the Sun card as carrying the Hebrew letter resh and the Star card the letter hey, and tied both to the idea of beginnings, breath and creative power. Gabe added that the number 93 stood out right away, noting that the Greek words for will and love share that value. Chance framed the episode as a spring equinox story about a cycle starting over."}, {"title": "Gematria Around 1893 and the Number 216", "body": "Chance Garton multiplied the digits of 1893 to get 216, which he linked to six times six times six and the magic square of the Sun. He said 1868 multiplies out to 384 and that 216 plus 384 gives 600, which he connected to an old idea of messiah cycles every 600 years. He also pointed to planks the characters walked past that he said carried the Hebrew value 600. Gabe linked 216 to the Analemma and to tax day, and Chance credited Gabe's earlier work on it. Both presented this as their reading."}, {"title": "Fisher King, Balder and Kang", "body": "Chance Garton compared He Who Remains to the Fisher King, a wounded guardian whose castle sits in mist, and said Loki played the fool who asks the question. He described the throughput multiplier as resembling a grail. When Loki mocked the Norse diorama, Chance retold the myth of Balder and the mistletoe spear and called it the same dying and returning king story. He also tied the name Balder to the bell of the Liberty Bell. Chance called the Balder and Liberty Bell link fun etymology."}, {"title": "The World's Fair and the Sacred Timeline", "body": "Chance Garton said the World's Fair was the natural place for a show about managing the story of history, and he noted textbooks of American history were first spread there. He questioned how large buildings could be built and removed so quickly but said he was not qualified to make a definitive statement. Gabe described the crane as a stage symbol of the god machine. Chance read the Liberty Bell inscription, tied to Leviticus 25 and the jubilee, as a sign of springtime and free will. Chance and Gabe also discussed voting booths and the Ivy League."}, {"title": "Victor Timely as Chronos and Victim", "body": "Chance Garton read the name Victor Timely as containing the word victim, and described him as a spring equinox figure matching the sacrificial ram, set against the scapegoat of the winter solstice. He said the word Chronos has a Greek gematria value of 510, the same value he found for the spelling of resh. Gabe argued that Mobius was meeting the shadow of his own past self, which Gabe called the rhetorician Phaedrus. Gabe also tied the Star card to the leap year, Pluto in Aquarius and a Capoeira pose."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: The next episode of Loki is incredibly dense and detailed with its numerical-linguistic encodings, this time focused on the Sun and the Star cards of the major arcana. The third episode of season 2, called "1893," leads us to Chicago's World Fair Exposition, one of the most significant events in the shaping of our modern historical mythos for America. The riddles are one hundred placent amazing, so don't miss out on this decode, even if you've not seen other episodes or watched the Loki TV Series.
fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "I like to peg two cards of the Major Arcana to each episode, it seems to really work out for me, and this time around I first thought it was gonna be the Hierophant because they were searching for this guy who's like you know the Pope of their TVA and all that, but I was wrong, it's the Sun.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Definitely the 93 stands out right away, that's the agape, and it's also will and love in Greek have an isopsephic value of 93. It's a big thing to the Thelemic order, and that's one of the foundations of the particular deck that we go through, but it was a sacred number before those orders came into it, those guys are latecomers to what 93 is really all about.", "author": "Gabe (Slick Dissident)", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/794d3a0b-c42b-4791-84c3-f79eff430f4c/SLICK-DISSIDENT.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Once you realize that the number of the beast or whatever is not talking about like the devil incarnate per se, other than that the Sun is the devil in wintertime when it kills off all the vegetation, it's actually a mystical number. It's about the formation of life, it's the cube of carbon, there's nothing really evil about it.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "It turns out February 29th, we're about 10 days away from the day of the offering. This is going to be the 366th day of the year and it's the extra day, and it's like the opposite of a day out of time. Other cultures remove a day, well for us we add an extra day in, and whether you accept that rhythm or not it's up to you.", "author": "Gabe (Slick Dissident)", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/794d3a0b-c42b-4791-84c3-f79eff430f4c/SLICK-DISSIDENT.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "There could not be a more significant and powerful image for sort of symbolizing everything in this episode. The first camera shot we open on this weather vane, first of all you can see based on the directions that are there that there's a wind blowing, and it's the west wind that's called Zephyr or Zephyrus.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Essentially the Fisher King is wounded by his own spear, allegorically. The wounding by his own spear is how the future version of Kang or He Who Remains is killed, by a wound that he suffers from Sylvie, who in a way is his own weapon because he created all the conditions for her to exist and laid the path out for Loki and Sylvie to find him.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Should we save Victor Timely? I mean, we need him to save us, but does that mean we just got our free will back, right? We just got free will because the old king is dead so we can do what we want, but are we trying to put in a new king and set it all up exactly like it was before and give up our free will?", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "The crane is the god machine. Whenever the end of the movie or the culminating situation needs to be explained, they just bring some strange contraption down, do some theatrical light flashing, and everybody says oh, ah, and then it doesn't even matter if plot actually resolves itself, it's the ooh in the ah that is where the sleight of hand takes place.", "author": "Gabe (Slick Dissident)", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/794d3a0b-c42b-4791-84c3-f79eff430f4c/SLICK-DISSIDENT.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "They are cheering for the outcome, for the allegory of the hero to rise or the savior to succeed. So I think maybe that's the same thing going on here, all of this play craft is a type of prayer initiation, but it may have taken a dark turn where we're praying for other things besides just the turning of the sun.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "It's heralding a new dawn or a new age of liberty like springtime does, these characters who now theoretically have free will. Liberty will, if B and W swap, free bell, free will, liberty free will bell, you see it's the same, it's the same word free will in Liberty Bell, and that's because the death of the old year or the original He Who Remains has removed the constraints.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "This may be one of my favorite things about the whole weave, is that I found out that Chronos in Greek, kappa rho omicron nu omicron sigma, equals in Greek gematria 510. So Mobius is in denial of his number one self, and here on this moment he's going to see the shadow of that self he is in denial of, and that is a rhetorician, somebody up on a stage who's a fast talker.", "author": "Gabe (Slick Dissident)", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/794d3a0b-c42b-4791-84c3-f79eff430f4c/SLICK-DISSIDENT.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}]
